messages:
Maya D: Quick thread — Prospect 'Aptiva Health' needs: redacted SOC2, ISO 27001 cert snippet, control mapping spreadsheet, and a signed pen-test authorization. Their third-party security firm wants to run authenticated scans against staging and possibly a one-night dedicated pool. They also require vendor COI (certificate of insurance) and vendor ATO. Who owns the signer and do we have a templated COI statement?

Noah R: We can provide redacted SOC2 and the ISO cert excerpt + control mapping. Legal signs the pen-test attestation; security provides the approved scope. We don't provide persistent host creds or raw host-level logs. COI: we can provide a standard statement confirming coverage limits, but we can't issue vendor insurance — buyer needs vendor COI.

Zara L: Operational constraints: we offer presigned S3 uploads for vendor scopes and short-lived jumpbox SSH tokens for authenticated scans. Direct root or host-level access is a hard no. If they require a warmed dedicated pool for the scan that's billed as a burst reservation. VPN access instead of IP allowlist adds ~1 business day of ops to set up.

Victor H: For the attestation signer, Legal (GC) can sign our standard pen-test letter. If the customer asks to widen indemnity or change liability caps, escalate to Execs. Also confirm whether the scans target an isolated tenant or shared staging — changes wording and risk.

Maya D: Buyer also asked for a quick ballpark: one-night 3x-A100 reservation + on-call ops support for the window. Any rough numbers to quote?

Zara L: Rough estimate: one-night 3x-A100 warm + ops = ~$1,600 total (infra ~$1,200 + ops scheduling & runbook support ~$400). If they want continuous monitoring during the scan add a small on-call surcharge. This is thumb rule — capacity team will confirm.

Noah R: Action items: 1) Maya to request vendor COI + ATO and upload to presign link. 2) Victor to prepare signature-ready pen-test attestation template (include short SLA line re: scoped window). 3) Zara to follow up with capacity for precise burst quote. 4) Ops Bot to create presigned upload and generate creds after approvals.

Ops Bot: Pre-signed upload created: https://uploads.redwood-inference.com/presign/aptiva-2829000001 (expires in 48 hours). Please upload vendor COI, ATO, and proposed scan scope to /aptiva/vendor-scan/.

Maya D: Uploaded vendor COI (pdf) and initial scope doc. I asked the buyer to confirm IP allowlist and whether vendor requires VPN.

Victor H: Draft attestation language I'll include: "Redwood Inference will limit testing to the agreed scope and timeframe; Redwood Inference will not accept responsibility for vulnerabilities identified outside the agreed scope. Any requests to expand scope or change liability will require written approval." Will have GC sign after buyer sends any redlines.

Zara L: Noted about VPN. If they request VPN instead of IP allowlist, ops estimate + scheduling moves the cost up by roughly one full day of engineering time (~$800 incremental). Flagging that for the buyer.

Noah R: Also requesting vendor insurance details is good practice — if vendor lacks sufficient coverage we may require additional indemnities. Ask them to include insurer name, limits, and expiry.

Maya D: Great, I'll update the buyer with the presigned link, preliminary ~$1.6k estimate, and explain potential VPN/setup surcharges. Tagging @Victor H and @Noah R for redlines as they arrive. Thanks! :thumbsup:
